sections.heading: C — Knowledge dossier: Space management and communication
sections.markdown:
## C — Knowledge dossier: Space management and communication

FACT_ID: sec15-F01 | anchor: A52
A side-space cushion leaves room to move right or left if needed. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F02 | anchor: A52
Avoid staying alongside another vehicle because its blind spot and a reduced escape space can expose you to a crash. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F03 | anchor: A52
Keep away from the centerline when possible to leave room from oncoming traffic. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F04 | anchor: A52
Help entering vehicles by changing lanes or adjusting speed when making room is possible. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F05 | anchor: A52
Give pedestrians and bicyclists extra space, especially children, and wait to pass in an adjacent lane rather than remain alongside. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F06 | anchor: A52
When a large vehicle passes, move toward the outside part of your lane to increase side clearance from it. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F07 | anchor: A52
On multilane roads, move ahead or fall back rather than remain beside a vehicle that may crowd your lane. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F08 | anchor: A52
Leave extra space beside parked cars because a person or vehicle may emerge. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F09 | anchor: A52
When positioned between hazards, split the available space but give more room to the more dangerous side. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F10 | anchor: A52
When approaching a bicycle and oncoming traffic together, slowing until the oncoming vehicle passes can let you pass the bicycle with more room. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F11 | anchor: A52
A steady speed and early slowdown or turn signals help a following driver maintain a safe gap. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F12 | anchor: A52
Pick up or drop off passengers in a safe place outside traffic when possible. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F13 | anchor: A52
Before parallel parking with approaching traffic behind, signal beside the space and allow following vehicles to pass first. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F14 | anchor: A52
Use the rightmost lane when slower than other traffic on a multilane road and pull aside safely if you are holding vehicles up. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F15 | anchor: A52
If tailgated and a right lane exists, move right; otherwise wait for a clear, legal passing opportunity before reducing speed gradually. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F16 | anchor: A52
Never brake abruptly to discourage a tailgater because doing so increases rear-impact risk. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F17 | anchor: A52
Allow large trucks and buses extra room because they cannot stop as quickly as a car. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F18 | anchor: A53
Pass only where signs or markings allow it and enough safe space exists, generally taking one vehicle at a time on the left. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec15-F19 | anchor: A53
Complete a pass promptly and return safely rather than lingering in the passing lane. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec15-F20 | anchor: A53
The handbook’s 55-mile-per-hour example allows about 10 seconds for passing and requires a corresponding oncoming gap and sight distance. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec15-F21 | anchor: A53
At 55 miles per hour, the handbook says each opposing vehicle travels over 800 feet in 10 seconds, requiring over 1,600 feet, about one-third mile, of combined clear distance. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec15-F22 | anchor: A53
Faraway vehicles may appear still or slower than they are, so wait to pass when the available gap is uncertain. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec15-F23 | anchor: A53
The handbook advises at least one-third mile, about 10 seconds, of visibility and no passing within that distance of a hill or curve hiding opposing traffic. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec15-F24 | anchor: A53
Do not pass where vehicles may enter or cross, including intersections, rail crossings and shopping-center entrances. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec15-F25 | anchor: A53
A vehicle being passed can block the view of road users or trains, and a turning driver may not expect a vehicle in the opposing lane. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec15-F26 | anchor: A53
The handbook compares a typical 15-foot car with a multi-trailer truck at least 75 feet long to explain why truck passing takes more time and clear road. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec15-F27 | anchor: A53
Before passing, look for pedestrians or cyclists, narrow lanes, ice, potholes or objects that could push another vehicle into the passing lane. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec15-F28 | anchor: A53
Do not pass without room to return to the normal lane, and never assume other drivers will create that room. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec15-F29 | anchor: A53
Do not pass with a rail grade crossing ahead. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec15-F30 | anchor: A53
Before returning after a pass, leave enough separation and ensure both headlights of the passed vehicle appear in the rearview mirror. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec15-F31 | anchor: A53
Give extra space to people who may not see you, including drivers with blocked views, reversing vehicles, obscured windows and pedestrians whose vision is obstructed or who use a white cane or guide dog. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec15-F32 | anchor: A53
Allow extra room or caution around potentially distracted delivery workers, construction workers, children and inattentive drivers. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec15-F33 | anchor: A54
Potentially confused road users include unfamiliar visitors, drivers searching for signs or addresses, unexplained slow drivers and pedestrians affected by alcohol. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec15-F34 | anchor: A54
Large trucks and buses need extra maneuvering room, including in roundabouts, and extra-wide loads need as much clearance as possible. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec15-F35 | anchor: A54
If another driver misjudges a pass or needs a sudden lane change, slow enough to let the driver return or merge safely rather than worsen the error. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec15-F36 | anchor: A54
Separate hazards when possible by adjusting timing so they are passed one at a time. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec15-F37 | anchor: A54
When simultaneous hazards cannot be separated, give the larger space cushion to the greater danger, such as an unpredictable child on a bicycle. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec15-F38 | anchor: A54
Headlights help others see the vehicle whenever visibility is poor, including rain, snow and fog. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec15-F39 | anchor: A54
The handbook recommends turning on headlights when the wipers are needed and when daylight begins fading. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec15-F40 | anchor: A54
Use headlights rather than parking lamps when driving requires lights, because parking lamps serve parked vehicles. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec15-F41 | anchor: A54
Use headlights when driving away from a low rising or setting sun so oncoming drivers facing glare can see the vehicle. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0054]

Misconceptions: A turn signal can mislead if activated before an intervening entrance; high beams are not appropriate in fog or close behind traffic; a truck’s high cab does not remove its blind areas.
Mnemonics: Use space, visibility, intention and timing as an authored communication cue.
Glossary: Separating risks means meeting hazards at different times; compromising space gives greater clearance to the more dangerous hazard; No Zone names a large vehicle’s blind areas.
Dynamic facts: Traffic gaps and visibility vary continuously; the passing-distance example and lighting descriptions do not guarantee every vehicle’s performance.

ranked.label: Pedagogic emphasis: Preserve side and passing space while using lights, horn and movement signals correctly.

items.why: Hazard spacing, passing gaps, lighting, horns and signals need separate decision scenarios.

corpus_stability.reason: The official dated snapshot is pinned, but revision frequency has not been measured. Unknown cadence remains blocked for release pending the section-A verification debt; this is not a claim that the handbook is volatile.
